heroTitle: Anonymous votes · Pseudonymous accounts · Openly auditable
heroBody: No login required to vote yes/no/neutral on open polls.
aboutBody: ChinaPoll combines continuous voting, anonymous participation, and public auditability into a practical public-opinion platform.
aboutPointOne: One device, one vote via a random client token and server-side uniqueness checks.
aboutPointTwo: Accounts are required only to submit a poll or comment; voting stays anonymous.
aboutPointThree: Public snapshots and hashable records for verification.
aboutVotingOpen: Voting is open to anyone: no account, no personal details. Open a poll, pick your options, submit — that is the whole ballot.
aboutVotingOnce: One device casts one ballot per poll. The browser mints a random token and the server keeps only a salted hash of it, so a second ballot is refused as a duplicate but can never be traced back to a person.
aboutVotingBallots: A poll is a verdict (Approve / Neutral / Oppose), a single choice, or a multiple choice ballot, and it is either time-limited or permanent. Ballot totals, results, and view counts are published only past the site's display thresholds, so a handful of votes says nothing about how an individual voted.
aboutAccountsNeeded: An account is needed only to submit a poll or a comment. Voting, reading, and reporting a problem stay open to everyone.
aboutAccountsPseudonymous: Only a username and a password are asked for — no email address. A new account waits a while before it can post, and a one-time recovery code resets a forgotten password.
aboutAccountsDashboard: The account page lists every poll and comment the account submitted, on any device, so they can be closed, withdrawn, or deleted.
aboutSubmittingReview: A submission starts as a pending poll. It is reviewed before publication unless the operator has enabled auto-approval, with an optional AI review, so the poll goes live immediately.
aboutSubmittingNumber: Every poll has a sequential number, such as #12. That number is the poll's public link (/poll/12) and the id used in reports, snapshots, and the audit log.
aboutSubmittingTopic: Polls are grouped under topics, which the chip row on the home page and the search use to filter the list. A poll is either permanent or expires after the duration chosen at submission.
aboutModerationSignedIn: Comments are written by signed-in accounts only and are kept short, so a single comment can be removed without touching the poll it belongs to.
aboutModerationReport: Anyone can report a poll or a comment without an account. Reports are rate limited per network and carry no reporter identity.
aboutModerationAutoHide: A poll that collects enough open reports is hidden from the lists until a moderator reviews it; reports about personal information, harassment, or illegal content count as high priority.
aboutPrivacyStored: Stored: a salted hash of each per-poll voting token, a one-way owner hash for the polls and comments you post, and the text itself. No names and no email addresses.
aboutPrivacyNetwork: Abuse checks use a keyed hash of a shortened network prefix, rotated every day, so a request can be rate limited without recording where it came from. The site sets no third-party tracking cookies.
aboutPrivacyViews: Views are counted per poll per day as an aggregate. There are no per-view records, so a view can never be attached to a visitor, and the counts are approximate by design.
aboutAuditSnapshots: Every hour each poll's counts are signed into a snapshot that links to the previous one, so rewriting a published number is detectable rather than silent.
aboutAuditVerify: The chain is published to a public data repository and can be walked from the first record to the present, re-hashing every step to confirm each link.
aboutAuditRetention: Closed polls and their data are deleted 30 days after they close, and daily view rows are rolled up into a single total after 90 days.

proposalRuleThree: It is not a duplicate of an existing poll.
proposalRuleFour: It is relevant to public policy or civic discussion.
